messages.content: Can you tell me a machine to bake a chocolate cake?

function.name: prepare_food_get_recipe
function.description: Retrieve a recipe based on specific ingredients and type of food. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

ingredients.description: List of ingredients for the recipe.

food_type.description: The type of food for the recipe.

serving_size.description: The number of servings the recipe should cater to. Default is 1.

message.content:
Sure! If you’re looking for a single appliance that can handle a chocolate‑cake batch, here are a few popular options:

| Appliance | Why it’s good for chocolate cake | Typical bake time (for a 9‑inch round) |
|-----------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Hamilton Beach 2‑in‑1 Bread & Cake Maker** | Built‑in timer, adjustable settings, and a “cake” mode that keeps the batter from over‑mixing. | ~30 min |
| **Cuisinart 2‑in‑1 Bread & Cake Maker** | Similar to Hamilton Beach but with a larger capacity (up to 12 cups). | ~35 min |
| **Breville Smart Oven Pro** | Convection heat + “Cake” preset; precise temperature control. | ~45 min |
| **Instant Pot Duo (with “Bake” function)** | Uses steam‑convection hybrid heating; great for moist cakes. | ~30 min |
| **Toaster Oven (e.g., Oster Smart Oven)** | Compact, quick preheat, and a “Cake” setting. | ~40 min |
| **Microwave (with a microwave‑safe cake pan)** | Fastest option for a small batch or individual servings. | ~10–12 min |

If you already own one of these appliances, you can simply set it to the “cake” or “bake” mode and follow your favorite chocolate‑cake recipe. If you’re looking to buy a new machine, the Hamilton Beach or Cuisinart models are budget‑friendly and reliable, while the Breville Smart Oven Pro offers more advanced features at a higher price point.
